data.summary: `ddflow wait --timeout 6297` prints 'waiting at most 1800s at a time; resume with the token to wait longer' and exits 2 after 1800s, but the token appears only under --json (wake.token); in text mode the advised resume is impossible, and the follow-up line says only to run `ddflow wait` again.
data.title: ddflow wait text output says resume with the token but never prints it

data.body:
Fixes bug B16e0083f21: `ddflow wait --timeout 6297` prints 'waiting at most 1800s at a time; resume with the token to wait longer' and exits 2 after 1800s, but the token appears only under --json (wake.token); in text mode the advised resume is impossible, and the follow-up line says only to run `ddflow wait` again. Found on PS-snapshot-calibrate.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B16e0083f21 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B16e0083f21 --regression-test <test>` first).

Not attached, they match nothing in the tree: ddflow/infra/store/snapshot.py, tests/test_snapshot_calibrate.py, ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.log.snapshot_max_mb.toml, ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_changed.log.snapshot.toml, ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_changed.log.max_cached_events.toml.
data.title: Fix bug B16e0083f21: ddflow wait text output says resume with the token but never prints it

data.summary: `ddflow claim PS-snapshot-calibrate --approval Q4623d7eb48` exited 3 for a live lease overlap (sw-fleet on DX-fleet-registry) and took nothing, yet recorded ask.consumed at 14:06:58 and `approvals show` reports 1/1 used; the refusal output never says so, the person's approval is lost and must be asked for again.
data.title: A refused claim spends the operator's one-use claim.force approval

data.body:
Fixes bug B6365c86730: `ddflow claim PS-snapshot-calibrate --approval Q4623d7eb48` exited 3 for a live lease overlap (sw-fleet on DX-fleet-registry) and took nothing, yet recorded ask.consumed at 14:06:58 and `approvals show` reports 1/1 used; the refusal output never says so, the person's approval is lost and must be asked for again.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B6365c86730 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B6365c86730 --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B6365c86730: A refused claim spends the operator's one-use claim.force approval

data.title: ci baseline runs on the branch's old merge base, not the main it merged with, so main's own failures read as new

data.text:
ci baseline runs on the branch's old merge base, not the main it merged with, so main's own failures read as new
PS-snapshot-calibrate ci at 34008a6b7 ran merged with main 702f0d225, but _pinned_base (ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py, from the B48c70b6773 fix) took merge-base(main, tree HEAD) on the unmerged worktree: e7d53a7c6, 299 commits behind. test_import_contracts, which fails on 702f0d225 and 9e959b771 without this item's code, was recorded 'new failure not failing on main' and ci went failed. The baseline should use the commit ci merged with (res.merged_with).

data.summary: Once the blocking lease went, `ddflow wait --item PS-snapshot-calibrate` answered 'Not waiting: lease has expired and is not handed on' at once with exit 2, the same code as 'still blocked, wait again'. A caller that retries on 2, as the output advises, spins: 399 instant calls in 40 minutes here. It needs its own exit code or a machine-readable reason.
data.title: ddflow wait exits 2 alike for still blocked and for an expired lease it will never wait on

data.body:
Fixes bug Be68798098a: Once the blocking lease went, `ddflow wait --item PS-snapshot-calibrate` answered 'Not waiting: lease has expired and is not handed on' at once with exit 2, the same code as 'still blocked, wait again'. A caller that retries on 2, as the output advises, spins: 399 instant calls in 40 minutes here. It needs its own exit code or a machine-readable reason.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Be68798098a --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Be68798098a --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug Be68798098a: ddflow wait exits 2 alike for still blocked and for an expired lease it will never wait on

chunk_findings.detail: `_discard_disabled_snapshots` gates the cleanup on `self.log_cfg.snapshot`, but the effective setting is `_snapshot_enabled()`: `SNAPSHOT_ENV` can switch snapshots on per process even when `[log].snapshot` is false (the new default). In that situation the branch still deletes every `read-snapshot*.bin` before the read that the environment switch is explicitly enabling, destroying the cache this run was meant to use. The docstring says “The per-process environment switch never does” this sweep, but the code does not consult `_snapshot_enabled()` or `SNAPSHOT_ENV`, so it does exactly the documented no-no.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_read.py:_discard_disabled_snapshots

chunk_findings.detail: The note tells users "Set log.snapshot = true to keep it; old snapshot files stay readable when it is on", but the new `log.snapshot_max_mb` cap added by the same change explicitly deletes "the oldest snapshots of other versions" when the cap is exceeded. So with `log.snapshot = true` and over 256 MB of old snapshots from other versions, old snapshot files do not stay readable/retained as promised.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_changed.log.snapshot.toml:4

chunk_findings.detail: The new `os.environ.get(SNAPSHOT_ENV)` directly reads the process environment. The r-adapters rule [r-adapters] puts environment access behind a port in ddflow/adapters; this direct stdlib read bypasses that port and prevents the adapter/fake seam, violating the rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_guard.py:_shard_meta

chunk_findings.detail: This diff does not fix the previously confirmed defect: the `why` line still says “old snapshot files stay readable when it is on and are deleted when it is off.” With `log.snapshot = true`, the new `log.snapshot_max_mb` cap can still delete oldest snapshots of other versions, so the promise remains inaccurate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_changed.log.snapshot.toml:why

chunk_findings.detail: The new effect says the shard facts “stay on unless log.reuse_parsed = false or DDFLOW_SNAPSHOT=0”, but `_guard._shard_meta` in this same change also returns `None` when `self.cache_writes` is false (a log built only to read another repository). The user-facing condition is incomplete, falsely promising the facts stay on in that read-only-repository case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_changed.log.snapshot.toml:effect

chunk_findings.detail: The test no longer isolates `L.SNAPSHOT_ENV`. If the test process inherits `DDFLOW_SNAPSHOT=0` in its environment, the assertion `EventLog(repo, "x", log_cfg=LogConfig(snapshot=False))._shard_meta() is not None` fails: by the change's own intent, `_shard_meta()` returns `None` under the environment kill switch even when the `[log].snapshot` knob is `False`. The test should use `monkeypatch.delenv(L.SNAPSHOT_ENV, raising=False)` to isolate the knob from the ambient kill switch.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_snapshot_calibrate.py:test_the_shard_facts_do_not_follow_the_snapshot_knob

evidence.budget_forced: code changed after the last round: main merged in (config_sections/log.py differs), README knob table and pins re-recorded, one constants exemption added

chunk_findings.detail: With `[log].snapshot = true` and enough events that `bytes_out + _SNAPSHOT_SLOT > cap` during the write loop, the new `raise ValueError("the snapshot is over [log].snapshot_max_mb")` escapes `_write_snapshot`. Nothing in this diff adds a `ValueError` handler, so the caller's read now aborts because the optional snapshot exceeded the file cap, rather than merely skipping the cache write. A log large enough to exceed the configured cap (for example lowering `log.snapshot_max_mb` below the default while leaving events high) will make the whole read fail.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_read.py:_write_snapshot

chunk_findings.detail: The new function gates deletion on `self.log_cfg.snapshot`, but the effective switch is `self._snapshot_enabled()` and the file imports `SNAPSHOT_ENV` for the per-process override. In a process with `[log].snapshot = false` but `SNAPSHOT_ENV` enabling snapshots, the first `_read` of a log dir passes the config check, adds the dir to `_SNAP_SWEPT`, and deletes all `read-snapshot*.bin` files; `_snapshot_enabled()` is still true afterward, so the persisted snapshot that the override promised is gone. The opt-in snapshot benefit is destroyed on the first read of every new process.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_read.py:_discard_disabled_snapshots

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier over-cap branch is unchanged: `mine.unlink()`, `_SNAP_COVERED.pop(...)`, and `total -= mine_size` are all inside one `with contextlib.suppress(OSError)`. If `mine.unlink()` raises `OSError` (for example a sibling process already removed `mine`, so this process gets `FileNotFoundError`), the subsequent lines are skipped while `total` still includes the current file's size. The later loop then sees `total > max_bytes` and unlinks every file in `others`, even though after excluding the missing current file the remaining files are under the cap, over-deleting valid snapshots.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_read.py:_collect_stale_snapshots

chunk_findings.detail: The bound check is still not atomic: `len(_SNAP_SWEPT) >= _SNAP_SWEPT_MAX`, the later `_SNAP_SWEPT.clear()`, and `_SNAP_SWEPT.add(self.dir)` are separate operations. Multiple threads with distinct `self.dir` can all read a length just below the maximum, skip the `clear()`, and then each add its own directory, overshooting the claimed bound by up to the number of concurrent readers. The intended bounded cache is therefore not actually bounded under concurrency.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_read.py:_discard_disabled_snapshots

chunk_findings.detail: The migration note says the per-shard append facts in `.ddflow/local/shardmeta` "stay on unless log.reuse_parsed = false", but the change itself makes `_guard._shard_meta` follow `reuse_parsed` and `cache_writes` only. For a configuration with `log.cache_writes = false` and `log.reuse_parsed = true`, the note tells the operator shardmeta remains on, while the new guard condition (both knobs) disables it. The note therefore omits `log.cache_writes = false` as another input that stops shardmeta, making the upgrade guidance incorrect/incomplete for that setting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_changed.log.snapshot.toml:7

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test still does not exercise the non-atomic bound it is meant to guard. With `_SNAP_SWEPT` at 255 entries, two distinct-dir readers interleaving their `len` checks before either `clear()` can both see `< _SNAP_SWEPT_MAX`, skip the clear, and then each add their own directory, so the set overshoots the bound. This test prepopulates 300 entries and calls `EventLog.read_all()` once from a single thread, so it never interleaves those operations and would still pass even with that race. The previous finding therefore remains unanswered.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_snapshot_calibrate.py:test_the_swept_set_is_bounded

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard adds a direct `os.environ.get(SNAPSHOT_ENV)` access in `_shard_meta`. Project rule [r-adapters] requires external dependencies, including environment access, to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`; this direct environment read in the log guard bypasses that port.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_guard.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: The updated knob doc says the per-shard append facts follow `reuse_parsed` and the environment switch below, but the corresponding `_shard_meta` guard also requires `self.cache_writes`. With `log.reuse_parsed = true` and `log.cache_writes = false`, `_shard_meta` returns `None`, so the facts do not stay on as this doc implies. The doc now misstates the actual conditions.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/log.py:56

chunk_findings.detail: The knob-only test asserts `_shard_meta() is not None` with `LogConfig(snapshot=False)` but does not clear `DDFLOW_SNAPSHOT` from the environment. Under the new behavior, `DDFLOW_SNAPSHOT=0` makes `_shard_meta()` return `None` regardless of the snapshot knob, so a test run or CI process that already exports `DDFLOW_SNAPSHOT=0` makes this test fail on exactly the single-threaded input the test uses. The old parametrized version controlled this with `monkeypatch.setenv`; the new test needs `monkeypatch.delenv(L.SNAPSHOT_ENV, raising=False)` before the assertion.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_snapshot_calibrate.py:test_the_shard_facts_do_not_follow_the_snapshot_knob

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier bound/atomicity finding is not answered by this diff: the test is left untouched and still prepopulates 300 entries, then calls `EventLog.read_all()` once from a single thread. It never interleaves the non-atomic `len(_parse._SNAP_SWEPT)` check, `_parse._SNAP_SWEPT.clear()`, and `_parse._SNAP_SWEPT.add(...)` operations, so multiple concurrent readers can still overshoot `_parse._SNAP_SWEPT_MAX` while this regression test passes.
